newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FUN IN BRUSSELS - ST. CATHERINE MODERN ART MARKET.
newsitem.headline: FUN IN BRUSSELS - ST. CATHERINE MODERN ART MARKET.

text.p: Exhibiting the work of young and upcoming artists' in a large prefab hall is a formula which has had enormous success in Paris, where the Grand Marche d'Art Contemporain (GMAC) market attracts 40,000 visitors a week.
Now the French organisers are to test the water in Brussels, with a first modern art market at Place du Marche aux Poissons behind the Saint Catherine Church.

Local Belgian artists are hesitant about the new formula -- only 10 of the 200 artists whose work is shown in the large hall that fills the former fish market square are Belgian. Most are French, with some English, German and African artists.

"This is a good market, nice audience, not as snooty as in Paris. Belgians have art in their blood," said Jacques van der Vaeren, a Belgian artist living in Paris who has exhibited in the Paris art markets.

Each artist has a small stand, showing a variety of works -- mostly paintings, but also sculpture and ceramics -- ranging in price from 10,000 to 100,000 francs. None of those exhibiting has museum status, but many of the pieces are excellent.
"This is an extremely useful formula. It's a way of seeing a lot of artists in a short time," said Martin Vaughn-James, a Brussels-based British artist.
Most of the artists are on site for the full six days of the market. Fabienne Vaerewyck, one of the organisers, said that the artists' presence was one of the market's main attractions.
"People can have direct contact with the artist, which is not often possible in a gallery."
In Paris, there are three markets a year, on Place de la Bastille and Quai Henri IV. A second modern art market in Brussels is planned for December.

PRACTICAL: The Modern Art Market is open daily from 1100 to 2000 from March 26-31. Vernissage and professional visits are on Wednesday, March 26 from 1800-2200. On Friday, March 28 there is a nocturne until 2200. Entry (at Bef 150) is right behind St Catherine Church, close to the St. Catherine subway stop.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
